title: Autonomous Galactic Survey Civilization - Technology Profile
description: Public edition: Coordinates long-duration probes and observational systems to map distant stars and planetary systems.
body:
Autonomous Galactic Survey Civilization. Coordinates long-duration probes and observational systems to map distant stars and planetary systems.

This database covers the technology as item 216 entry 65 of Manon's "100 Technologies Beyond Omega (B)" catalog, section "Stellar and Interstellar Expansion". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: theoretically plausible. Surveys map the galaxy (Gaia); autonomous probe coordination is unproven.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

description: Public edition: Coordinates long-duration probes and observational systems to map distant stars and planetary systems.
body:
Known science foundations of Autonomous Galactic Survey Civilization.

Gaia mapped a billion stars. But coordinating long-duration probes and observatories as an autonomous survey civilization is a vision.

Key quantity check (Stars mapped by Gaia in billions / stars mapped by probes): computed ratio 2 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.4. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Autonomous Galactic Survey Civilization - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Coordinates long-duration probes and observational systems to map distant stars and planetary systems.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Autonomous Galactic Survey Civilization.

Probes are slow and few. Coordination adds complexity. The science case vs cost is debated.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 9.3 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is gaia vs probes at 9.3 orders of magnitude (gaia larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

body:
Candidate approaches for Autonomous Galactic Survey Civilization, ranked by the weighted rubric 0.5*maturity - 0.25*cost - 0.25*risk:

1. Astrometric surveys (maturity 4/5, cost 3/5, risk 1/5; score 1).

2. Long-duration probes (maturity 2/5, cost 4/5, risk 3/5; score -0.75).

3. Autonomous coordination (maturity 1/5, cost 2/5, risk 4/5; score -1).

Top-ranked approach: Astrometric surveys. Rankings are comparative planning aids, not predictions of success.

Unresolved problems for Autonomous Galactic Survey Civilization, in priority order (research burden index 22, 2 blocking):

Cost (severity 3/3, tractability 3/3, BLOCKING; priority 6).
